page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance utilizes a dedicated Intel processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8). Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags, alongside integer and bit manipulation features like BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1684.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core and memory performance are relatively limited. The stress-ng multi-core score is 1714.68, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 2251.0, both falling into the weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth is also low, with uncached read and write speeds at 19.35 GB/sec and 12.78 GB/sec respectively.

Given its hardware profile, the n4-standard-2 offers an entry-level general-purpose resource density. It is appropriate for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, single-threaded text processing, and simple background tasks. It is less applicable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded software compilation, or complex mathematical simulations due to its constrained multi-core performance and memory bandwidth.
